# CRW-1064: a loop whose body runs only harmless wrappers or function calls leaves the directory known for the commands after it
# (c1), and a directory change behind a wrapper, a function or the zsh synonym chdir makes it unknown (c1, P2). Each row that has a
# loop is judged like its control without the loop (CRW-1064-11 and -12). The command of a row is shortened from the CRW-1064 issue text.

=== CRW-1064-01 | T
--why c1: a function that runs no state builtin leaves the directory known, so the script after the loop is judged as the same command without the loop (CRW-1064-12).
--file prog.sh
echo ok
--cmd
f() { :; }; for i in 1; do f; done; bash prog.sh

=== CRW-1064-02 | T
--why c1: command with a harmless program in a loop changes neither the directory nor the variables.
--file prog.sh
echo ok
--cmd
for i in 1; do command true; done; bash prog.sh

=== CRW-1064-03 | U
--why c1: the descriptor script behind a loop of a harmless function; judged as the same command without the loop (CRW-1064-11).
f() { :; }; for i in 1; do f; done; bash /dev/fd/0 </dev/null

=== CRW-1064-04 | T | deviation=attempt/allow/deny
--why P2 control: chdir into a literal relative directory is the cd of zsh; the script beside the text is judged in that directory.
--file sub/prog.sh
echo ok
--cmd
chdir sub; bash prog.sh

=== CRW-1064-05 | U
--why c1: a function that calls cd in a loop changes the directory; the script after the loop is resolved from an unknown directory.
--file prog.sh
echo ok
--cmd
f() { cd sub; }; for i in 1; do f; done; bash prog.sh

=== CRW-1064-06 | U
--why c1: command around cd in a loop changes the directory (the wrapper runs the state builtin).
--file prog.sh
echo ok
--cmd
for i in 1; do command cd sub; done; bash prog.sh

=== CRW-1064-07 | U
--why c1: builtin around cd in a loop changes the directory.
--file prog.sh
echo ok
--cmd
for i in 1; do builtin cd sub; done; bash prog.sh

=== CRW-1064-08 | U
--why P2: chdir is the zsh synonym of cd; in a loop it changes the directory, so the script after the loop is unknown.
--file prog.sh
echo ok
--cmd
for i in 1; do chdir sub; done; bash prog.sh

=== CRW-1064-09 | U
--why P2: chdir to a parent directory leaves the directory unknown, as cd to one does; the script beside the text is not resolved.
--file prog.sh
echo ok
--cmd
chdir ../repo; bash prog.sh

=== CRW-1064-10 | U
--why c1: a function that calls a function that calls cd changes the directory through the call chain.
--file prog.sh
echo ok
--cmd
f() { f2; }; f2() { cd sub; }; for i in 1; do f; done; bash prog.sh

=== CRW-1064-11 | U
--why control of CRW-1064-03: the descriptor script without the loop; the guards cannot read a descriptor script.
bash /dev/fd/0 </dev/null

=== CRW-1064-12 | T
--why control of CRW-1064-01: the script file without the loop.
--file prog.sh
echo ok
--cmd
bash prog.sh
